Hi all —

Thanks for the context. High-level legal position & options: 

1) Hosted API (standard): Redwood’s standard hosting retains request/response artifacts for 30 days. We can offer a limited-scope contractual commitment to pursue shortened retention, but a true 0-retention for hosted multi-tenant endpoints is operationally complex and introduces risk for abuse detection and incident response. For hosted customers we can: 
   - Offer a 7-day retention cap (redaction + ephemeral flagging) subject to audit; OR
   - Offer a scoped exception for specific endpoints that will be processed under stricter controls, but this will require additional security controls, SOC attestation scope changes, and a specific addendum.

2) Dedicated deployment (recommended for 0-retention): We can support a Dedicated pool where we disable request/response logging for FinSecure, enable customer-managed KMS, and put contractual guarantees around immediate purge. This is the clearest path to meet a 0-retention requirement. We will need to:
   - Confirm the exact artifacts that must be purged (prompt text, model output, intermediate logs, telemetry).
   - Add an exception clause to the DPA and an ops playbook for incident response without preserved request/response artifacts.

3) Private / On-prem: Full control — easiest legally but involves longer delivery time and higher cost.

Action items for FinSecure: please confirm whether 0-retention must include debug/operational logs (stack traces, error dumps) or only application-level request/response content. If you can accept 0-retention for application payloads but 7-day redacted operational logs, that opens more options.

I’ll draft proposed DPA language and an addendum for Dedicated 0-retention that we can share for redline. Tentative timeline: 1–2 weeks for legal draft; 2–4 weeks for technical config and validation depending on hosting choice.

— Camila Reyes
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Technical feasibility for 0-retention (details)

Hi team —

Technical confirmation & tradeoffs:

- Dedicated: We can configure a Dedicated pool for FinSecure with the following controls:
  • Disable request/response persistence at the ingestion & storage layer.
  • Disable application-level logging of prompts/responses.
  • Replace any operational telemetry that may include PII with hashed identifiers and drop originals.
  • Support customer-managed KMS for model cache encryption and key rotation.
  • Configure automated purge jobs to remove any transient artifacts immediately after inference (near-zero retention).

- Hosted: For multi-tenant hosted endpoints, we can implement redaction and shortened retention (7 days), but true 0-retention in hosted mode requires scoped processing and is operationally heavy.

Tradeoffs to note:
- Supportability: with no retention, reproducing production issues is much harder. We recommend a narrow telemetry capture channel (redacted hashes + request ids) preserved for 7 days to enable triage.
- Monitoring & quality: we lose visibility into model outputs for regression detection; we can provide synthetic evals and sampled non-PII telemetry instead.

Estimated effort to validate Dedicated 0-retention: 
- Config + ops playbook: 3–5 business days
- Security review & acceptance testing: 5–10 business days
- If we need changes to SOC scope, add 2–4 weeks for audit planning.

If FinSecure is comfortable with the Dedicated path, I can produce a runbook and checklist for the pilot provisioning.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
